questions.question: Audio features come from a frequency view of the waveform, not the raw samples. What transform produces that view?
options: Sorting samples by size
Averaging all samples together
Decomposing the signal into frequency components
Deleting every second sample
questions.explanation: Frequency decomposition reveals structure time samples hide. This lesson builds the Fourier view behind audio features.

questions.question: What does the coefficient X[0] represent for a real signal under this DFT convention?
options: The highest oscillation frequency
The DC component, equal to the sum and proportional to the mean
Only the imaginary part of the signal
The phase of the Nyquist component
questions.explanation: At k=0 every factor is 1, so X[0] is the sum of samples. Dividing by N gives the mean under the usual normalization.

questions.question: Which sign and scale reconstruct the signal in the inverse DFT?
options: Use the same sign and multiply by N
Discard all negative frequencies with no conjugate symmetry
Use the opposite exponential sign and divide the sum by N
Take the absolute value of each coefficient
questions.explanation: The forward transform uses a negative sign in the exponent; the inverse uses a positive sign and the 1/N normalization.

questions.question: How does the convolution theorem compute a discrete convolution with FFTs?
options: Add the two spectra and take a second forward FFT
Multiply the time-domain samples only at equal indices
Take the determinant of the two Fourier matrices
FFT each input, multiply the spectra pointwise, then apply the inverse FFT
questions.explanation: Circular convolution in the time domain corresponds to pointwise multiplication in frequency. Padding handles linear convolution when required.

questions.question: For N=8 samples, which bin is the Nyquist frequency?
questions.explanation: The Nyquist bin is N/2 for even N, so k=4. Frequencies above it alias into lower frequencies.

questions.question: Why is an FFT preferable to the direct DFT for a long sequence?
options: The FFT removes the need for complex arithmetic
Cooley-Tukey reduces typical work from O(N^2) to O(N log N)
The DFT cannot represent phase
The FFT always returns exact real numbers
questions.explanation: The FFT reuses subproblems in the DFT sum. It preserves the same frequency information while reducing computational cost for suitable lengths.
